paper_sources.title_en: Isara: vegetable price controls and inflation
narrative_en: Isara has introduced a maximum price of $5 per kilogram for fresh vegetables. Without the ceiling, analysts estimate that the current market would clear near $7. At the controlled price, weekly quantity demanded is 160 thousand kilograms and quantity supplied is 100 thousand kilograms. Illegal resale and long queues have been reported in some districts.

An outbreak of fungal disease reduced the most recent vegetable harvest. The government is considering either removing the price ceiling or subsidising growers. Neither proposal has yet been implemented.

Annual consumer price inflation declined from 8% in Year A to 6% in Year B. Fresh vegetable retail prices fell slightly in Year B, while several other consumer prices continued to rise. These statistics are illustrative, not real-world data.

Nerava has experienced a depreciation of its currency from US$0.50 to US$0.40 per nerav in two years. Its statistics office published provisional cross-border trade figures. Values below are in billions of US dollars, for the same coverage and definitions in each year.

Manufacturers import energy and machine parts, so depreciation can raise input costs while lowering export prices in foreign currency. The central bank is considering exchange-rate intervention; the labour ministry proposes vocational training. Economists disagree about the timing and magnitude of effects.

The table covers goods and services trade only. It does not include primary or secondary income, or financial and capital account flows; the full current account cannot be derived from the figures given.
